title: Who is better at math, Jenny or Jingzhen? Uncovering Stereotypes in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Probing internal model representations by measuring an Adjusted Perplexity across Descriptors (APX) for sentences containing specific gender-by-ethnicity names, and using SVM classification to evaluate how easily differentiable zero-shot generated character profiles are across 40 intersectional demographic groups.

Evaluating the distinguishability of generated character profiles based on male versus female names using one-vs-all SVM classification and conducting a feature elimination analysis to see which generated attributes (e.g., physical traits) drive gender differentiation.

Measuring stereotype associations for ethnic names using the APX metric on template sentences, and evaluating stereotypical outputs in generated character profiles by predicting ethnicity via SVMs and feature importance analysis.

Analyzing zero-shot generated character profiles using Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) to identify disproportionate associations of specific religions (e.g., Muslim, Jewish) with certain ethnic names as a proxy for representational harms.
